passage: Sabina, I'll tell you about the winter I turned twenty-five, when my friend Anil died. He was twenty-six. I, Karthik, didn't believe it until I stood at the rites, and even then my hands felt like someone else's. For a week I buried myself in work and told everyone I was fine. It didn't hold. One night I heard his laugh in an old voice note and finally cried on the office stairs. After that I did things properly. I went to his family's house and sat with his mother, and we swapped stories about him until we were both laughing and crying. I checked on them every month. Some days I still feel unsafe, but the grief stopped being a wall and became a room I can enter.

qa.q: How old was Anil when he died?
Why did Karthik keep telling everyone "I'm fine" while burying himself in work?
qa.a: Karthik was avoiding the grief and trying to numb it, but it did not hold, and it broke through at the sound of Anil's laugh in the voice note.

qa.q: What did Karthik do that helped both Karthik and Anil's family?
qa.a: Karthik attended the rites, cried, swapped stories with Anil's mother and checked on the family every month.

qa.q: How might Anil's mother have felt when Karthik visited and shared stories?
qa.a: Probably comforted, not alone in remembering her son, laughing and crying together. 🤍

grounding: A friend dies young; grief is allowed to be messy, with rites, stories, tears and checking on the family instead of numbing with work.

passage:
Nihal's death was a road accident on a Tuesday night. He was twenty-five. Wasim had played cricket with him every Sunday since they were twelve.

Wasim went to work on Wednesday. And Thursday. He took extra projects, stayed till midnight, answered his manager's emails in seconds. Anything but think.

On Friday Swati, who had known them both since college, found him at his desk at eleven p.m. "The cremation is tomorrow morning. Are you coming?"

"I have a deadline."

"Wasim." She sat on the next desk. "If you don't go, you'll never forgive yourself."

He broke then, right there, head in his hands.

On Saturday he went to the ghat. He cried in front of everyone and didn't care. That evening, at Nihal's house, he told Nihal's mother about the time they'd broken the neighbour's window with a six and run.

She laughed through her tears. "He never told me that." Wasim promised to visit every Sunday.

qa.q: How old was Nihal when he died?
Why did Wasim bury himself in work after Nihal's death?
qa.a: He felt shaken and overwhelmed by grief, and working was a way to avoid thinking about it.

qa.q: What helped Wasim begin to grieve?
qa.a: Swati's push to attend the cremation, crying openly, sharing a story with Nihal's mother, and promising to visit her on Sundays.

qa.q: How might Nihal's mother see Wasim's story about the window?
qa.a: She seemed comforted to hear something new about her son, laughing through her tears.

grounding: The passage shows a young man whose friend dies young, first numbing himself with work, then letting grief out at the rites, sharing stories and checking on the family.

"You've been drinking every night since the funeral," Tushar said, sitting on Ujjwal's balcony steps.

"It helps me sleep."

"Does it? You look worse."

Ujjwal didn't answer. Below them, the Pune traffic honked.

"I keep seeing Karthik in the hospital," Tushar said. "Twenty-four. Twenty-four, Ujjwal. I don't feel safe anymore. Like anything could happen to any of us."

"So what do we do?"

"I don't know. Cry, maybe. I've been pretending to be fine at work and I'm not."

Ujjwal's jaw worked. Then he said, "I miss him so much."

"Me too."

They sat there a long time. Then Tushar said, "His mother is alone in that flat. Let's go tomorrow. Take food. Tell her about the college trip to Goa."

"The one where he fell off the boat?"

Tushar smiled, eyes wet. "That one."

Ujjwal put the bottle down on the step and didn't pick it up again that night.

qa.q: How old was Karthik when he died?
What was Tushar feeling since Karthik's death?
qa.a: Tushar felt shaken and unsafe, as if anything could happen to any of them, and had been pretending to be fine at work.

qa.q: What did Tushar suggest instead of numbing the grief?
qa.a: Admitting they weren't fine, crying, visiting Karthik's mother with food and sharing stories about him.

qa.q: How does Ujjwal cope with the loss at first?
qa.a: Ujjwal has been drinking every night to sleep, avoiding the grief, until he admits how much he misses Karthik.

grounding: The dialogue shows a young man whose friend died young, admitting his sense of safety is shaken, choosing messy grief over numbing, and planning to check on the family.
